title: Stability
hookLine: Benedictines vow to stay in one community for life

cards: A new monk stands in the chapel in front of the whole community. In his hand is a promise he has written out himself, and he lays it on the altar. Benedict's Rule says what goes in it.
He promises obedience. He promises to keep turning his life toward God. And he promises something that sounds, to modern ears, almost impossible.
He promises to stay. Not to stay a monk anywhere things feel right. Here, with these brothers, under this roof.
No moving on when the abbot gets on his nerves or the brother in the next stall hums off key. The Rule's Latin word for that promise: stabilitas.

teach.b: Stabilitas. Stability. To see why Benedict cared, look at his very first chapter.
He describes different kinds of monks, and the ones he's hardest on are the wanderers. They drift from monastery to monastery, a few days here, a few days there, never settling, always guests.
In the Rule's picture, they follow their own wishes and never stay long enough for anyone to know them. Benedict's answer is the vow to stay.

teach.h: THE TOOLS OF THE SPIRITUAL CRAFT.
teach.b: Later, after a long list of what he calls the tools of the spiritual craft, things like don't return evil for evil, love your enemies, don't give up on God's mercy, he says where those tools get used.
The workshop, he says, is the enclosure of the monastery and stability in the community. That's the surprise. Stability isn't a reward for being holy.
It's the workbench. In this picture, patience gets learned with people you can't leave, and forgiveness gets tested by staying near the person you need to forgive.
Move on every time it gets hard, and the tools never touch the wood. There's an old line in the Bible that sounds like this vow, though it comes from a different story.

teach.h: WHITHER THOU GOEST, I WILL GO.
teach.b: Ruth, a widow, refuses to leave her mother-in-law, and says, "whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge." Stability is that kind of loyalty, given to a place and a people.

how: Benedictine monks and nuns make a vow of stability that ties them to a particular community; Benedictine oblates living outside the monastery can take stability as a call to stay faithful to their own family, parish and place.

o: the promise to stay with one community
a calm mind that is never upset
a monk's vow to own nothing at all

games.q: what the Rule says about staying — tap the pairs.
p: whither thou goest, I will go

s: stability means a monk can never leave the building
it's a promise to stay with one community; the Rule pictures that community as the workshop.
the monk lays his written promise on the altar
the Rule has the new monk write out his promise and place it on the altar.
Benedict praises the monks who wander from house to house
he's hard on them: they never stay long enough to be known.

games.q: you're a young monk. the brother in the next stall drives you up the wall, and a monastery down the road looks calmer. what does the Rule ask?
o: stay, and let this be the workshop.
stay, but stop speaking to him.
games.why: Benedict says the workshop for the tools of the spiritual craft is stability in the community. the hard brother is part of the work.

practice: Sit where you are and notice the urge to move, to check the phone, shift your weight, get up for something, and don't follow it.

Then bring to mind one place, one job, one relationship you'd like to walk out of today, and picture yourself staying a little longer, feet on the floor, without fixing anything; if you pray, bring that place to God by name.
Staying never means staying where you're being hurt: if you're in danger, call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Stabilitas. The Benedictine promise to stay with one community, so that the hard work of love has somewhere to happen.

orig.note: Latin, from the Rule of Saint Benedict: stability, staying put in one community.

carryVoice: Your line: stay. In Benedict's picture, the workbench is the place you didn't leave. Until tomorrow.
